title: Comment on PR-018, what it saves "What it saves": Hard to read from the table format. lead and toolsmith do investigate, do workaround and do long-term fix

messages.text: Hard to read from the table format. lead and toolsmith do investigate, do workaround and do long-term fix

You are right: the 'What it saves' rows pack too much into one cell. I sent it to the lead and the toolsmith.

- Cause: each row holds the claim, before and after numbers, a tag (OBSERVED), the test driver and a long note, all in one line.
- Workaround: the proposal author rewrites the rows as: what, before, after, better or worse, one short line.
- Long-term: the Proposals page shows the details folded away, and refuses rows over a length limit.

What you need to do: nothing.

**The PR-018 numbers will be rewritten in a simple form, and a tool will keep every proposal that way.**

- **Now (workaround):** the menu fix's author rewrites the next version's "What it saves" with 4 short columns (what / before / after / better, same or worse), at most 5 rows. Notes go below the table.
- **Long term:** a tools helper (the answer-format checker) makes the proposal tool refuse crowded rows and fold the notes behind "details" on the Proposals page.
- The new version comes with the glide numbers (rev 4 keeps the normal glide). I'll post here when it's up.

What you need to do: nothing.
